newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Borsodchem placement draws high demand.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Borsodchem placement draws high demand.

text.p: The international private placement of Hungarian chemical company Borsodchem shares attracted $70 million worth of orders, lead managers told a news conference on Wednesday.
The strong demand allowed organisers to set a very favourable subscription price, they said.

"There was such strong demand that the issue could be priced close to the prevailing market price," Christian Hess, corporate finance official at WestMerchant, one of the international lead managers, said.
Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt offered 1.2 million Borsodchem shares in the second phase of the company's privatisation and raised 3.53 billion forints or $22.2 million.
The subscription price was set at 2,940 forints/share and $18.50/Global Depositary Receipt on Monday.
Last Friday Borsodchem closed at 2,985 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange and was quoted at $19.00 on the SEAQ.
"This placement was the most tightly priced issue yet to come from central and eastern Europe," Hess said.

Borsodchem CEO Laszlo Kovacs did not predict profits for this year but said the company would pay dividends after 1996 results, in addition to a 10 percent extraordinary dividend advance for 1996 that shareholders had approved this summer.
"We will certainty pay a dividend after 1996 and our dividend policy is unchanged," Kovacs said.

Kovacs said Borsodchem was increasingly able to distance itself from the PVC cyclical effects, thanks to increasing capacity of MDI (methylene dyphenil diisocyanate) of which Borsodchem is the only producer in central Europe.

Borsodchem's increased PVC capacity is already operational with an annual 250,000 tonnes compared with 210,000 tonnes earlier, while all of the higher MDI capacity will be operational in two weeks. Borsodchem raised its MDI capacity by 33 percent to 32,500 tonnes.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Borsodchem shares closed at 3,150 forints, up 50, on Wednesday.
